newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to take B Band bids on March 31 - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to take B Band bids on March 31 - ministry.

text.p: The Brazilian government said it will take bids March 31 from consortia interested in operating cellular services on the B Band frequency.

The Communications Ministry said in a notice published in the government's official gazette bid specifications for auctions on 10 B Band concessions will be made available to interested bidders on Monday.

The tender documents, containing base prices and other bidding details, will be avaliable for 200 reais at the ministry on Monday from 0900-1200 local/1100-1400 gmt and from 1400-1700 local/1600-1900 gmt, the notice said.
B Band bids will be received at 0900 local/1100 gmt on March 31 and must include proposed prices for the right to operate concessions and proposed tariffs, it said.
Consortia planning to bid also must present qualifying documents the same day and winning bids will be those which contain the lowest proposed tariff and highest concession price, it added.
The selloff of B Band concessions is being closely followed by investors and the financial market as it will mark the first opening of Brazilian cellular telephone services to foreign capital.
So far, some 20 foreign-led groups have expressed interest in bidding on the concessions, the federal government's first step toward privatizing Brazil's massive and promising telecoms sector.
In a decree published December 30, the government outlined the 10 areas nationwide where it will offer 15-year B Band concessions.
The government hopes to grant concession contracts by mid-1997.
